title: How Near-Death Experiences Work
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss near-death experiences (NDEs). They open with the Pam Reynolds case, a singer who underwent a hypothermic cardiac arrest procedure for a brain aneurysm and later described details she could not have seen. They cover the term coined by Dr. Raymond Moody in Life After Life, the earliest description in Plato's Republic (the soldier Er), the classic NDE hallmarks (calm, light, tunnel, out-of-body experience, spirits, life review), "bad trip" hellish NDEs, prophetic visions of the world ending in the 1980s, Gallup and Proctor polling statistics, Kenneth Ring's research on post-NDE changes, the film Fearless, and comparisons to PCP and ketamine. They then contrast supernatural explanations with scientific hypotheses (oxygen deprivation, visual cortex misfiring, neural noise, endorphins, spatial sense malfunction) and close with a listener email from Jeff in Sydney about a stomach herniation surgery.

segments.title: Pam Reynolds story and opening banter
segments.summary: The hosts open by recounting Pam Reynolds, a singer who had a brain aneurysm operation involving hypothermic cardiac arrest, and who later described seeing her grandmother, a tunnel and white light, and details of the surgery she could not have seen.

segments.title: Origins of the term and early accounts
segments.summary: Dr. Raymond Moody coined the term near death experience in his book Life After Life. The hosts note the earliest description in Plato's Republic, about the soldier Er, and discuss Albert Brooks films about the afterlife.

segments.title: Common NDE hallmarks and bad trips
segments.summary: The hosts list common features: calm, bright light, tunnel, out-of-body feeling, spirit beings, communication with spirits, and life review. They also discuss negative hellish experiences and 1980s prophetic visions of the world ending.

segments.title: Polling statistics and research
segments.summary: The hosts cite a Gallup and Proctor poll from Adventures in Immortality showing percentages of NDE features and bad trips, the finding that religious belief had no clear effect, and Kenneth Ring's findings on changed attitudes toward life and death.

segments.title: Fearless film and drug-induced comparisons
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the film Fearless and its portrayal of post-NDE feelings, then compare NDE-like experiences to PCP and ketamine trips, which they say undermines the supernatural view.

segments.title: Supernatural versus scientific explanations
segments.summary: The hosts contrast the supernatural explanation of a soul leaving the body with scientific hypotheses: visual cortex misfiring, neural noise, spatial sense malfunction, endorphins, and oxygen deprivation. They note science may explain the how but not the why.

segments.title: Further reading and sign-off banter
segments.summary: The hosts point listeners to related HowStuffWorks articles on near death experiences and out-of-body experiences, then joke about a choking experiment they do not endorse.

segments.title: Listener mail: Jeff's stomach surgery
segments.summary: Listener Jeff from Sydney writes about a surgery in which most of his stomach was pulled through a diaphragm hole and had to be removed, with the esophagus attached to the small intestine. He is recovering well.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The episode closes with a brief sign-off and a reminder to visit HowStuffWorks.
